title: Separating Proxy Smoothing from Weak Overlap in Proximal Operator Compactness

proof_attempt_summary: The first proposal embedded a probability-capped inverse problem in a positive two-proxy proximal law, but its compactness came from vanishing treatment overlap and its minimax geometry was already the bounded-reward OPE truncation geometry. A root-changing revision proved an overlap–proxy obstruction and an exact ancillary-kernel OPE transfer for the constructed subexperiment; the reviewer and an independent validity gate agreed that this remains an example-specific, letter-scale diagnostic. A field-level successor would need either a general Blackwell/Le Cam characterization with non-ancillary boundary cases or a genuinely proxy-driven uniformly overlapping construction and frontier.
tldr: The proposal asks when compactness of the usual treatment-arm proximal operator reflects proxy smoothing and when it merely reflects weak treatment overlap in an observed shared covariate. The candidate separation theorem shows that on \(H_J=\{v(W,J)=g(J)\}\), \(\|Tg\|^2=E[\bar e(J)g(J)^2]\); therefore uniform overlap on an infinite-dimensional \(L_2(P_J)\) rules out compactness. In the explicit positive two-proxy design, the restricted singular tail is exactly \(\sqrt{e_j}\), and the Bernoulli perturbation likelihood is deficiency-zero equivalent to known-behavior bounded-reward OPE because \(W\) has a parameter-free conditional kernel. The old three-regime rate is retained only as an OPE-transfer corollary. The proposed novelty is the structural impossibility of conflating shared-covariate overlap with proxy compactness and the exact proximal-to-OPE transfer, not the polynomial exponent.
gap: Spectral proximal analyses can assign a compact tail to a conditional-expectation operator without separating the invariant subspace generated by an observed covariate shared by both proxies. In the supplied witness, this omission led a weak-overlap spectrum and a familiar bounded-reward OPE frontier to be described as weak-proxy behavior.
fill: Prove the exact norm and approximation-number obstruction for general observed-stratum operators; then prove two-way deficiency-zero equivalence for the explicit positive complete latent lift. Use the prior fixed-design frontier only to demonstrate the consequence of the transfer and formulate the residual question after overlap directions are separated.
